## Read the record behind the product name

A 510(k) clearance, a De Novo authorization, and premarket approval are distinct regulatory pathways. Use the language appropriate to the actual record. The book's inherited chapter heading “FDA-cleared AI products” is a convenient category heading; individual tables explicitly identify De Novo records rather than calling every authorization a clearance.

Start with the submission number, device name, intended use, indications, compatible inputs and hardware, user population, and limitations. Then determine whether the local workflow matches those conditions. Do not attach a later product-family claim to an earlier submission merely because the names are similar.

| Claimed role | Question to resolve |
|---|---|
| Triage or notification | Does it change worklist priority, and what diagnostic review remains required? |
| Detection assistance | What findings, images, users, and reading configuration are supported? |
| Acquisition guidance | Which views and hardware are covered, and who judges adequacy? |
| Quantification | What is measured, in which units, and what diagnosis is not established? |
| Autonomous screening | Which population, acquisition, target condition, and no-result pathway are specified? |
| Image enhancement | Which acquisitions and quantitative or diagnostic claims are supported? |

The [FDA AI-enabled device list](https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/artificial-intelligence-enabled-medical-devices/list-artificial-intelligence-enabled-medical-devices) provides a broader discovery resource and explains that it is not comprehensive. Use its submission links and the applicable current labeling when evaluating a real deployment. Authorization does not eliminate the need to verify interoperability, local workflow, training, monitoring, and change management.

Absence from this appendix means only that no example has been curated here. It is not evidence that a modality lacks authorized devices. Products outside the United States require review under the relevant jurisdiction rather than extrapolation from this index.
